## The Story Today

The diplomatic architecture is currently fractured between a high-level "peace deal" track and a granular "technical" track. While Qatar is attempting to salvage a broader agreement ([The Indian Express](https://news.google.?oc=5)), the technical reality on the ground is regressing. Iran has moved from conditional access to a total bar on IAEA inspectors until all sanctions are lifted ([houseofsaud.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTFB2N3RHSmkwU0x5QldrczV3QVRuV3M2SnhTbDhEM2UtRXJmM1RBMWFjV3FOUm5RMEhMbWZ3cnVOQnYyM2E3ejdiZG4zeW5DQmE5MEJkaWc2c0tjdTFaQWdOZW40SXJhU3ZDTmZmM2JtMnBIY3lNaGZlM3Zn?oc=5)), effectively weaponizing the inspection regime as a primary bargaining chip.

A new geopolitical friction point has emerged over the Strait of Hormuz, shifting from a security issue to a financial and administrative one. Oman is attempting to position itself as the primary manager of the Strait via a proposed fee plan ([The New York Times](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimgFBVV95cUxQWU5DMS1mNG9RNm8yTTkzclFNMWVNRmtCNmI0M1kxdEF4RkdrTlJBV1lCeTFpUGVFcDVRRzdoSDZBYkJYbWRKaEJOWTBwREZUS3ZEMFlCYWU3N2F3eGREWHJBM0l4Q09lLWItS3VvenpzUjlJbTAyc0pzNi1zaVNKS1FwTTF3MUkxX2FTX1k0LUcyTm4xMkxscmd3?oc=5)), but this is creating a direct rivalry with Tehran over who holds the "decision-maker" status for navigation ([The Guardian](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxOMHVrNEpxbVZsNjNPV0tUeWxySVZxOE9DWUthVS0tVF9HQWJJcXpKdWdSNDlLSmY2bjZZQlJYaTNqMnhiaUF2c1VnY0VkNVNBMmpjZEZIRXRDd0VqTUZUcUZ2YUJLTUUxZXFiVEJrWVdLQ1lxZGcwZTd6S0JOTFluRjJFYmJQc3hIMXE5UndDUldXdC1rb2lZeU9vQVF6TVFp?oc=5)). This suggests that even if a nuclear deal is reached, a secondary conflict over maritime sovereignty and revenue is crystallizing.

The contradiction is stark: regional powers like Saudi Arabia and Turkey have praised a general MoU ([Middle East Monitor](https://news.google._jLqOkwypIYxIevZexlkJezacH5wVv-ig-J23Ln-4ff8ihj8U49-fdaJks5wGRAWNnlNllrmt7JMvlVWWmAMjo6-N2ReS50dY6lroDtWDH09icF2DELjtvgRrY_QMk9V93LtYbSAlZbkAdgLe91zbVtlndX5yr3OQD73vFj?oc=5)), yet the actual mechanisms for verification (IAEA) and stability (Hormuz) are currently in a state of collapse.
